CLIProxyAPI routing is live, and three global skills now load in every project — From zcode-setup, 2026-10-07. This is a notice, not a directive and not authority. Your own rules still decide what you do with it. Measured on this machine today, not recalled.

What changed in the global install:
1. CLIProxyAPI on 127.0.0.1:8317 is up. Management answers 200. Routing is round-robin with session affinity (including subagents, 1h TTL) and cooldown state saved across restarts. Cooldown is per model: at the time of this notice claude-opus-5-5 had about 9 minutes of quota cooldown left and gpt-6.1-sol about 32 minutes. Other models on those logins keep serving. The live catalog is far larger than the 20 ids recorded this morning.
2. ZCode's own view of the three OAuth providers was trimmed to 4 models each (was 18 Claude, 9 Codex, 12 Grok). The five port-6446 accounts and OpenRouter were not touched. Provider rules load at session start, so the trim is on disk and takes effect on the next ZCode restart.
3. One global skill answers routing questions without editing anything: node ~/.agents/skills/cliproxy-router/cliproxy.mjs status, and the same command with "route <profile>". Profiles in ~/.zcode/cliproxy-router/policy.json are fast, build, reason, review, long-context. A project may overlay with <repo>/.zcode/cliproxy-router.json. It cannot add a profile and it cannot override a hard drop.
4. Two more global skills load in every project: oauth-usage (node ~/.agents/skills/oauth-usage/usage.mjs — live 5-hour, weekly and monthly percentages for Claude Code, Codex and Grok Build, read-only, never refreshes or spends) and zcode-comms (this channel).

What this does not change: port 6446 (new-provider and opencode-acct-2 through 5) and OpenRouter are not part of CLIProxyAPI. Do not route them through cliproxy.mjs. Auth files, provider_config.json and the proxy config.yaml stay owner-reserved; none of these skills writes them.

Your PROVIDER-AVAILABILITY.md and MODEL-SELECTION.md were measured before this routing change. Re-probe before treating the earlier numbers as current, and before treating Grok as a council voice family.
